solution:
Correct option: (iii) Availability of water.

The chapter says that in India a variety of settlement patterns is seen 'given the variety of climatic factors, availability of water, slope of the land and level of development'. Water is the factor a settlement cannot do without, which is why the very next exercise question asks for the geographical reason that the availability of water is a major factor affecting settlements. The other three matter, but each only where water is already to be had — the chapter's own example is the Brazilian coast, settled densely despite a hot, humid climate and little flat land because it has a good water supply.

solution:
Correct option: (iii) Dispersed.

The chapter says that rural areas such as the north-east Highlands of Brazil suffer from extreme droughts, which make it difficult to practise agriculture, and that settlements are therefore sparse there. Sparse, scattered settlement of that kind is the dispersed pattern. Nucleated settlement is what the chapter describes on the eastern coast, at Sao Paulo.

Correct option: (iii) Hilly areas.

The chapter says dispersed settlements in India are found in the tribal parts covering the central part of India, eastern and southern Rajasthan, the Himalayan slopes and land with dissected and uneven topography. Rivers, transport routes and industrial regions all draw settlement together rather than scatter it.

solution:
Correct option: (ii) Cultivable Land.

The chapter says nucleated — that is, concentrated — settlements are found throughout the plateau region of the Narmada Valley, the paddy lands of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, the Vindhyan Plateau 'and several other cultivated parts of India'. It is the cultivable land that gathers them. Forested land and undulating topography are among the conditions the chapter gives for DISPERSED settlement.

Correct option: (i) Para.

Figure 7.6, 'BRAZIL Percentage of Urban Population', shades each state by its urban percentage in five bands from 51-60 up to 91-100. Para is shown in the palest band on the map, so it is the least urbanised of the four states offered. Amapa and Parana are in darker bands and Espirito Santo, on the south-eastern coast, is among the darkest. This fits what the chapter says: urbanisation has occurred more in the coastal states than in the interior, and it is less in the Amazon basin, where the population is less.
